title: US State Plane Helper: Zones and Workflow
description: Understand State Plane zones and units; this coordinate workspace does not identify zones or convert State Plane values.
summary_sentence: For example, a Denver GPS point belongs to Colorado Central (zone 0502) — and knowing the zone, the datum and the unit before touching a converter is ninety percent of State Plane competence.
quick_answer: State Plane coordinates depend on a zone, datum and unit. This workspace does not identify State Plane zones or convert State Plane coordinates.
steps_intro: Use the workspace for supported global formats; determine the zone, datum and unit using authoritative documentation before using validated GIS or NGS tools.

body.t: A deliverable labelled State Plane needs its zone, datum and units identified from reliable metadata or authoritative sources. This workspace cannot identify the zone. The
Bearings and distances on American surveys ride State Plane grids. Knowing the zone and its unit decodes the document's numbers.
Full State Plane conversion belongs in validated survey or GIS tools. Identify the zone, datum and units separately; this workspace does not determine them.
Each zone is a small projection tuned so distortion stays under one part in ten thousand — the design bargain this page explains before any number moves.

Many states publish in US survey feet, some in international feet, some in metres. The two 'feet' differ by two parts per million — invisible across a garden, a metre across a state. Naming the unit is the helper's first commandment.
States wider than tall get Lambert zones stacked north–south (California has six); tall states get Transverse Mercator columns (Illinois has three). The map of zones is the states' shapes, projected.

faq: Old surveys ride NAD27, whose coordinates can sit hundreds of metres from NAD83's for the same ground. The document's era decides; conversions between them are datum shifts, not arithmetic.
State Plane bearings are grid bearings; convergence (the angle between grid and true north) grows toward zone edges. Surveys state their basis of bearings — read it before comparing to a compass.

Grid distances are projection distances; ground distances at elevation shrink or stretch by the combined factor. At Denver's altitude the difference is roughly 1 part in 4,000 — surveyors live by it, walkers may ignore it.
Original 1986, HARN, NSRS2007, 2011 — each nudged coordinates by centimetres to decimetres. Metadata is the only way to know; the helper teaches you to ask.
No. This workspace neither identifies State Plane zones nor converts State Plane coordinates. Use NGS NCAT or validated GIS with the correct zone, datum and unit.
Hawaii and Alaska have multiple State Plane zones. Consult authoritative zone documentation; this workspace does not select zones.
UTM is one-size federal; State Plane is tailored — distortion budgets an order tighter, units matched to local law, and a century of records written in it. American land work speaks SPC.
